claims.statement: The data plane splits into packages/sandbox-runtime (provider-agnostic Python code that runs inside every sandbox: process tree, boot sequence, control-plane protocol, OpenCode integration, JS tools/plugins) and per-vendor infra packages (modal-infra, e2b-infra, daytona-infra, opencomputer-infra) that never implement agent behaviour but package sandbox_runtime into a vendor image/template; only modal-infra additionally exposes the HTTP control surface the control plane calls.

Every infra package stages packages/sandbox-runtime/src/sandbox_runtime at /app/sandbox_runtime with /app on PYTHONPATH (OpenComputer writes it under the non-root user's ~/app and symlinks /app there), because OpenCodeServer loads tools, plugins, skills, bin scripts and /app/opencode-deps from those hardcoded absolute paths — an image staging the package elsewhere boots a supervisor that silently installs no agent tools.

entrypoint.py is both the CLI and the production composition root: build_supervisor() consumes process secrets into a frozen RuntimeConfig and constructs every concrete service (RepositoryBoot with tunnel env/hooks/synchronizer, OpenCodeServer, AgentBridgeProcess, CodeServer, WebTerminal, BrowserDesktop, optional ManagedSkillsMaterializer); main() installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that only set a shared asyncio.Event, then either runs the supervisor or hands control to Modal's token-gated image-build protocol.

The agent bridge runs as a separate child process (`python -m sandbox_runtime.bridge` spawned by AgentBridgeProcess with sandbox/session/control-plane/token/opencode-port args and merged stdout forwarding), so a bridge crash is an observable process exit the supervisor can restart, and exit code 0 is treated as a deliberate graceful exit that shuts the whole sandbox down rather than restarting.

SandboxSupervisor.run() fixes normal-session ordering: boot mode resolution, tunnel prep, stale boot-warning file removal, browser desktop (best-effort), RepositoryBoot.boot, managed-skills materialization, code-server (best-effort), web terminal (best-effort), OpenCode server, then the agent bridge, then monitor_processes; optional-service failures are logged and stopped while OpenCode/bridge failures propagate to the fatal path, and shutdown runs in a finally block stopping services in reverse dependency order.

monitor_processes() applies an explicit per-component restart policy against MAX_RESTARTS=5, BACKOFF_BASE=2.0, BACKOFF_MAX=60.0: repeated OpenCode or bridge crashes are fatal (report then set shutdown_event), while code-server, ttyd/ttyd-proxy and the VNC stack exhaust non-fatally; OpenCode restarts reuse the boot-captured repository list and workdir and must not re-run managed-skills materialization, so restarts do not depend on control-plane availability.

Fatal in-sandbox failures are reported by POSTing {error, fatal:true} to {CONTROL_PLANE_URL}/sessions/{id}/sandbox-error with the sandbox bearer token and X-Sandbox-ID header, truncating to the last 1000 chars with 3 attempts and 2^n backoff; reporting is skipped entirely when control_plane_url or session_id is absent, so a repository-less sandbox still boots and fails only in its logs.

BootMode (fresh / snapshot_restore / repo_image / build) is derived from IMAGE_BUILD_MODE, RESTORED_FROM_SNAPSHOT and FROM_REPO_IMAGE, re-exported as OPENINSPECT_BOOT_MODE for hooks, and it decides severity: git sync failure or timeout is fatal in fresh and build modes but only a recorded boot warning on restore/repo-image, setup.sh aborts a build but degrades to a warning on a fresh session, and start.sh failure aborts only when it is the primary repository.

Provider tunnels are resolved outside the sandbox and handed in through /workspace/.tunnels.env (TUNNEL_SANDBOX_ID plus TUNNEL_<port>=<url> lines); because that write can land before the entrypoint starts, the supervisor keeps a file whose marker matches its own SANDBOX_ID and deletes everything else (snapshot/repo-image leftovers with dead URLs), then waits for every EXPECTED_TUNNEL_PORTS entry to appear before running start.sh so a start hook can reference its public URL.

RepositoryBoot is the single authority for the /workspace checkout layout: it validates SESSION_CONFIG repository entries as safe path segments and writes the canonical ordered manifest to /tmp/oi-repo-manifest.json plus a generated /workspace/AGENTS.md for multi-repo sessions; the bridge's push targeting, git-signing per-repository config, and the JS create-pull-request tool all read that manifest instead of re-deriving the path convention.

AgentBridge connects to wss://.../sessions/{id}/ws?type=sandbox with a bearer sandbox token and X-Sandbox-ID, emits a ready event carrying the image-baked SANDBOX_VERSION and per-repository baseSha, drains queued boot warnings into warning events exactly once (never replayed on reconnect), runs a 30s heartbeat, and dispatches prompt commands as background tasks so push/stop/snapshot/shutdown/ack/refresh_diff stay responsive on the same socket.

Prompt handling splits transport from policy: OpenCodeClient owns HTTP/SSE wire concerns against the localhost OpenCode server, while OpenCodePromptStream owns lifecycle policy (SSE inactivity timeout, max prompt duration, cleanup budget) and translates OpenCode events into control-plane events keyed by the control plane's messageId, using a self-supplied ascending OpenCode user-message ID for parentID-based attribution.

The bridge derives its maximum prompt duration from SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 7200) minus a snapshot reserve of min(900s, 25%), so an agent turn is forced to terminate before the provider kills the sandbox and the control plane retains time to snapshot.

Sandbox pushes execute a provider-generated push spec (targetBranch, refspec, remoteUrl, optional repoOwner/repoName, force): the named repository is resolved against the supervisor manifest and the matched entry's path is used verbatim so a crafted spec cannot select a checkout outside the session, git stderr is credential-redacted, and every outcome funnels through one push_complete/push_error emitter.

BufferedEventForwarder is the reconnect-safe delivery state machine: execution_complete, error, snapshot_ready, push_complete and push_error are critical events stamped with a deterministic ackId that stay pending until the control plane acks and are re-sent on reconnect, everything else is at-most-once, and with no bound socket events enter a 1000-entry buffer that evicts the oldest non-critical event first, with all recovery flushing serialized by one lock so nothing is sent twice.

HTTP 401/403/404/410 from the WebSocket handshake raise SessionTerminatedError and a non-retryable GitSigningError is likewise terminal: the bridge stops retrying and exits cleanly with code 0, which the supervisor reads as a graceful bridge exit and shuts the sandbox down rather than crash-looping against a control plane that has already forgotten the session.

Git credentials inside a sandbox are brokered per request rather than captured at spawn: the /usr/local/bin/oi-git-credentials shim execs sandbox_runtime.credentials.git_credential_helper, which speaks git's credential protocol to the control plane, caches to /run/oi/scm-creds.json (0600, advisory lock) with a 5-minute refresh buffer, and never uses the cache as a fallback for a failed refresh; only when there is no control-plane context (image builds) does it fall back to the injected one-shot VCS_CLONE_TOKEN.

Commit signing is control-plane-brokered: GitSigningRuntime fetches per-session SSH signing config and writes gpg.format=ssh, gpg.ssh.program=<bin dir>/oi-git-sign and user.signingkey into each repository checkout, oi-git-sign POSTs the bounded payload to /sessions/{id}/commit-signing, and per-prompt authorship comes only from the command's explicit author.gitIdentity (agent-only or attributed-user with strict name/email parsing, never inferred).
RuntimeConfig rejects any CONTROL_PLANE_URL that is not HTTPS except loopback development hosts at composition time, so the sandbox refuses to carry its bearer token over plaintext.

The agent-facing JS tools (spawn-child, send-child-prompt, get-child-status, cancel-child, slack-notify, create-pull-request) are a separate surface from the Python modules: they ship as data inside sandbox_runtime, are copied into <workdir>/.opencode/tool/ at boot, execute under OpenCode's Node/Bun runtime, and call the control plane's HTTP API directly via the shared _bridge-client helper rather than talking to the bridge process.

Child-session tools define the agent's delegation surface: spawn-child POSTs /children and is explicitly restricted to affirmative user requests for a separate child sandbox (not sub-agents or subtasks); send-child-prompt queues behind current child work; get-child-status is dual-mode list/detail with optional response and paginated trajectory; cancel-child cancels nested children by default.

slack-notify is the one env-gated agent tool: it is skipped unless AGENT_SLACK_NOTIFY_ENABLED=true (which the Modal manager sets from the control plane's agent_slack_notify_enabled flag), and it converts non-OK responses into a structured {ok, reason, agentMessage} envelope whose REASON_GUIDANCE keys are kept hand-symmetric with SLACK_DENIAL_REASONS in @open-inspect/shared because the shipped file cannot import workspace code.

OpenCode plugins are a third surface deployed conditionally by the supervisor: provider-token-broker.js is a provider-neutral single-flight client for POST /sessions/{id}/provider-auth/{provider}/access-token with a 5-minute pre-expiry refresh buffer, and codex-auth-plugin.js / xai-auth-plugin.js are copied into .opencode/plugins/ only when OPENAI_OAUTH_MANAGED / XAI_OAUTH_MANAGED are set, overriding OpenCode's built-in auth because project plugins dedupe by provider id (last wins) so rotating refresh tokens persist centrally instead of dying with the sandbox.

Files in sandbox_runtime/bin are standalone CLIs (upload-media.js, oi-git-sign) installed into OPENINSPECT_BIN_INSTALL_DIR (default /usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin on OpenComputer) and must never be placed in .opencode/tool/, because OpenCode import()s every file there during tool discovery and would execute module-level code with the parent's argv.

modal-infra/src/app.py defines the modal.App and its three secrets — llm-api-keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, injected into sandboxes but never into snapshots), github-app (used server-side to mint installation tokens, not injected into sandboxes), internal-api (MODAL_API_SECRET) — plus two images, with function_image bundling the sandbox_runtime source tree at /root/sandbox_runtime so the control-plane-facing modules can import it at runtime.

validate_control_plane_url is Modal's anti-SSRF boundary: it compares the parsed netloc including port against the comma-separated lowercased ALLOWED_CONTROL_PLANE_HOSTS env var and fails closed — an unset or empty variable rejects every URL with a security.hosts_not_configured warning — while empty/optional URLs pass; web_api applies it to control_plane_url on create/restore and to both image-build callback URLs.

src/images/base.py builds the sandbox image: pinned opencode-ai/@opencode-ai/plugin (never below 1.18.15, where OpenCode's wrapping 48-bit message-ID counter breaks turn ordering), code-server, checksum-verified ttyd, agent-browser plus Chromium, the X11/VNC/noVNC stack and account/init helpers, a pre-built /app/opencode-deps tree also baked into the global OpenCode config dir so boot-time staging skips a multi-second arborist reify, system-level git credential.helper configuration that applies before the entrypoint runs, and CACHE_BUSTER taken from RUNTIME_VERSION rather than a hand-maintained number.

manager.py funnels both create and restore through one _launch_sandbox parameterized by a three-variant image source (_BaseImageSource, _RepositoryImageSource setting FROM_REPO_IMAGE/REPO_IMAGE_SHA, _SnapshotImageSource setting RESTORED_FROM_SNAPSHOT plus a compatibility clone token), assembling the full env contract while filtering user env vars through _RESERVED_LAUNCH_ENV_VARS so a repository secret can never impersonate a manager-owned variable.

Modal's manager owns port exposure: raw VNC 5900 is never exposable even when a user requests it as an extra tunnel, settings.tunnelPorts are validated (integer, 1-65535, max 10) and deduplicated against reserved service ports, and each resolved tunnel URL is popped as a service URL only if that service owns the port — otherwise a user's own 8080 with code-server disabled would be misreported as code_server_url; leftover URLs go both into /workspace/.tunnels.env and the returned SandboxHandle.

ModalBuildSessionService owns image-build sandboxes through an identity-bound tagged lifecycle (create/start/snapshot/terminate); every operation after create re-reads the sandbox tags and raises BuildSessionNotFoundError unless both openinspect_kind=image-build and the matching build id are present, so a stale or forged provider session id cannot snapshot or terminate someone else's sandbox, and user env vars are scrubbed of reserved callback keys before launch.

Modal image builds start dormant: the sandbox launches with --await-modal-image-build-token-stdin-v1 and blocks reading stdin until the control plane has persisted the build-to-provider-session binding and calls api-start-build-sandbox, which writes a 64-hex callback token; the token is length-bounded and pattern-validated, consumed into a RepoImageBuildCallback whose callback env vars are then popped, and start refuses delivery when the tag's launch protocol differs.

RepoImageBuildCallback.from_env detects build-callback configuration by env-var presence rather than truthiness and raises RepoImageCallbackMisconfigured on a partial set, so a misconfigured image build aborts with a nonzero exit instead of running with completion reporting silently disabled and wedging the control-plane row in `building` until the provider timeout reaper fires.

web_api.py is the HTTP surface the control plane calls at https://{workspace}--open-inspect-{endpoint}.modal.run: seven POST endpoints plus an unauthenticated GET api-health, each running inside _execute_endpoint which performs HMAC auth first and emits one modal.http_request log line; auth is Bearer <unix-ms>.<HMAC-SHA256 hex> against MODAL_API_SECRET with a 5-minute window, where a missing secret is 503 and a bad token is 401.

Modal request models use strict=True with extra="ignore" so a newer control plane can add fields without breaking an older deployment, and the create path reconstitutes a typed SessionConfig before re-serializing it into SESSION_CONFIG — new wire fields must be added to SessionConfig or they silently never reach the sandbox, while restore paths use extra="allow" to preserve unknown nested keys.

web_api adds IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_GRACE_SECONDS (10 minutes) on top of the build-execution budget for the provider session timeout, because the filesystem snapshot is taken after the build sandbox finishes; Modal's limits and grace are pinned against the TypeScript declarations by contract tests.

modal-infra/deploy.py exists to eagerly build base_image against the looked-up deployed app before `modal deploy`, so the first session does not pay the image build; src/app.py must never be deployed directly because only src/__init__.py (or deploy.py) registers the function modules.

e2b-infra, daytona-infra and opencomputer-infra are build-time-only packages: the control plane talks to those vendors' REST APIs at runtime and execs `python -m sandbox_runtime.entrypoint` with per-sandbox env after creating the sandbox, so no template starts the supervisor itself.

e2b-infra splits responsibility between e2b.Dockerfile (pinned toolchain layers, a site-packages .pth so the credential helper resolves /app without PYTHONPATH, system-level credential shim, world-writable /workspace and /tmp/opencode, and deliberately no SANDBOX_VERSION since E2B drops Docker ENV) and build-template.py, which stages sandbox_runtime, applies .copy/.set_workdir/.set_start_cmd, and keeps an inert `sleep infinity` start command solely so the READY_CMD finalization check can fail a broken toolchain at build time; it then pre-warms one sandbox to dodge a vendor slow-first-spawn bug.

daytona-infra builds a named base snapshot with the same pins and /app/sandbox_runtime staging as Modal and registers python -m sandbox_runtime.entrypoint as its entrypoint; bootstrap.py is the CLI and on --force polls until a deleted snapshot is no longer returned by the API (up to 300s) because Daytona's delete() returns before the backend removes it, so an immediate recreate fails with 'Snapshot already exists'.

opencomputer-infra/src/build-template.ts is the TypeScript builder: it stamps SANDBOX_VERSION from the imported runtime manifest, installs everything under the non-root sandbox user's HOME with /app symlinked there and OPENINSPECT_BIN_INSTALL_DIR=~/.local/bin (the reason that env-var exists instead of a hardcoded /usr/local/bin), and pins two build-time failure modes — npm's no-lifecycle-scripts default requiring --allow-scripts=opencode-ai, followed by an `opencode --version` assertion so a stub binary can never ship silently.

Each infra package is rebuilt by a Terraform null_resource/local-exec keyed on a source hash over the infra directory plus packages/sandbox-runtime/src, so a runtime change rebuilds the template; the policies diverge materially — Modal, E2B and OpenComputer hash every file the image bakes (skill Markdown included) while daytona.tf filters to *.py/*.js/*.ts, so a skill-only change does not rebuild the Daytona snapshot — and OpenComputer derives its snapshot name from the hash so each build is immutable.

runtime_manifest.json is the single source of the runtime generation (runtimeVersion, generation, minimumCompatibleGeneration, minimumRebuildGeneration) and runtime_manifest.py raises at import if the v<N> prefix and generation disagree; it is consumed by value from the Modal cache buster, the control plane's rebuild policy (images below MIN_REBUILD_RUNTIME_VERSION get rebuilt as runtime_incompatible without invalidating ones still safe to boot), and the OpenComputer builder, so the numeric generation is one shared sequence across all providers.

The runtime version the control plane trusts is the one the sandbox reports, not the one baked into a Dockerfile: the bridge copies the image's SANDBOX_VERSION into its ready event, which is why providers that do not propagate image ENV (E2B, OpenComputer, Vercel) re-export SANDBOX_VERSION in create/exec env derived from the manifest.

sandbox_runtime/image_build_callback_env.json is the single declared source of the cross-plane image-build env-key contract (callback env names, build-mode and timeout vars, and the intentionally divergent reserved sets); production code on both planes keeps its own constants and only tests read the file, pinning Modal's Python constants against it.

These Python packages share one lint scope: each pyproject extends the root ruff.toml, the root lint-staged glob covers exactly packages/{daytona-infra,e2b-infra,modal-infra,sandbox-runtime}/**/*.py with ruff check --fix and ruff format, and eslint.config.js deliberately ignores packages/sandbox-runtime/** because its JS runs under Node inside sandboxes rather than in the TypeScript project.

ci-python.yml runs a lint job for sandbox-runtime and a second over packages/modal-infra, e2b-infra and daytona-infra, pytest jobs for both, and `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` for the JS tool/plugin surface that ships inside the Python package and has no npm workspace to run in; both mypy jobs are continue-on-error, so typing is aspirational rather than gating.
